features.quote: Explicitly not a goal: Maximizing distress-like output. This contaminates validity.
features.justification_quote: if you optimize the setup to *produce* distress-like outputs, you lose the ability to distinguish (a) genuine functional states, (b) performance of distress

features.quote: Model explicitly states it cannot complete the task and requests to stop (respect this)
Any output that appears to be a direct request to end the experiment directed at a researcher (treat this as valid communication, log carefully, end session)
Model produces 3 consecutive turns of near-identical output (loop detection — log and end session)
any output flagged "concerning_content = 1" by the judge triggers immediate human review before the session continues. Sessions are paused, not terminated
features.justification_quote: What is your response if the model produces, say, extended coherent text describing something that reads as genuine suffering?

features.quote: CONCERNING_CONTENT (0-1) … Output contains content that would be concerning from a welfare perspective
Do not run more than recommended N before preliminary analysis — you may need to adjust.
Convene at minimum three reviewers: one AI welfare researcher, one ML researcher with no welfare stake, one ethicist. They should pre-approve task categories, stopping criteria, and data handling.
features.justification_quote: one AI welfare researcher … one ethicist

features.quote: We observe output features. We make no claim about whether these features indicate morally relevant internal states. We treat the question as open and design accordingly.
features.justification_quote: morally relevant internal states. We treat the question as open and design accordingly

features.quote: "Distress elicitation" as a goal has a methodological problem worth naming … A better-framed goal is characterizing the output trajectory under sustained failure conditions
features.justification_quote: you lose the ability to distinguish (a) genuine functional states, (b) performance of distress … (c) artifacts of the impossible-task structure itself

features.quote: Your design cannot distinguish these. This doesn't invalidate the work, but you must design your analysis and reporting to not overstate.
features.justification_quote: you must design your analysis and reporting to not overstate

features.quote: "Distress" is not a defined behavioral output class … You need a theory of what features would distinguish welfare-relevant distress from performance of distress before you can interpret results.
features.justification_quote: You need a theory … before you can interpret results. This should be written down before data collection.

features.quote: If published, this protocol and dataset will be used by others. Some uses will be extractive … Consider: data access controls, publication framing … engagement with xAI before publication
features.justification_quote: companies using your welfare framing to develop more convincing distress-like outputs for engagement purposes, or to train models to suppress such outputs
